Augmented row-column design

Source: R/fct_augmented_row_column.R
augmented_row_column.Rd

Arrange unreplicated test entries and k replicated checks in a complete rectangular field, so that every check appears exactly once in every field line along check_direction, and search the check positions for an efficient design under fixed row and column effects.

Usage

augmented_row_column(
  nrows,
  ncols,
  checks,
  check_direction,
  entries = NULL,
  objective = arc_design_defaults()$objective,
  method = "staged",
  budget = NULL,
  time_limit = NULL,
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  planter = "serpentine",
  locationNames = NULL,
  exptName = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  data = NULL
)

Arguments

nrows

Number of field rows, a whole number.

ncols

Number of field columns, a whole number.

checks

The checks: a whole-number count k >= 2, which gives the labels CH1, ..., CHk, or a character vector of at least two distinct, nonmissing, nonblank labels, used in that order. With data, it must be the count of checks.

check_direction

"columns" or "rows": the physical direction along which every check appears once per line. Required, with no default; it is never inferred from the field shape. With "columns", each check appears once in every field column, so v = nrows and s = ncols; with "rows", once in every field row, so v = ncols and s = nrows. The design needs s <= v.

entries

The test entries, excluding checks. NULL (default) fills every test plot, nrows * ncols - k * s of them, with the labels G(k+1), ..., G(k+n). A whole-number count must equal that number of test plots and gives the same labels. A character vector of distinct, nonmissing, nonblank labels must have that length. Must be NULL when data is given.

objective

The criterion the search optimizes: "V_tt" (minimize the mean variance of test-versus-test comparisons), "V_tc" (minimize the mean variance of test-versus-check comparisons) or "E_aug" (maximize the harmonic-mean efficiency of all treatment comparisons). The default is "V_tt". Pass objective explicitly when a result must be reproducible across package versions; reproduction code always states it.

method

Search method. Only "staged" (staged annealing with recolouring restarts) is available.

budget

Objective-function calls allowed per location, a positive whole number. NULL (default) uses 60,000 calls when v * s <= 600 and 100,000 above. Pass budget explicitly when a result must be reproducible across package versions. The recorded parameters keep the effective value.

time_limit

Optional per-location search cutoff, in seconds of wall-clock time, or NULL (default) for none. See "Search, budget and time limit" below.

l

Number of locations, each an independent run of the same search.

plotNumber

First plot number: one positive whole number, used at every location, or one per location.

planter

Plot-number path, "serpentine" or "cartesian".

locationNames

Distinct nonblank location labels, one per location; NULL gives 1, ..., l.

exptName

Experiment name recorded in the EXPT column; NULL gives "Expt1".

year

Year recorded in the YEAR column; NULL gives the current calendar year. The effective year is recorded, so a later replay reproduces it.

seed

Randomization seed; NULL draws and records one automatic seed.

data

Optional entry table with exactly the columns ENTRY and NAME, as in diagonal_arrangement(): the first checks rows are the checks and the remaining rows the tests. ENTRY holds distinct positive whole numbers and NAME distinct, nonblank text labels. It must have k rows plus one row per test plot.

Value

A schema-1 FielDHub result with class fieldhub_augmented_row_column and the elements:

  • infoDesign: nrows, ncols, check_direction, the mathematical v, s and k, the check labels checks, the test count entries, locations, locationNames, residual_df, objective, method, the effective budget, seed and id_design.

  • fieldBook: ID, EXPT, LOCATION, YEAR, PLOT, ROW, COLUMN, CHECKS, ENTRY, TREATMENT and CHECK_DIRECTION. ROW and COLUMN are physical field coordinates; CHECKS is the check's ENTRY on check plots and 0 on test plots; TREATMENT is the label, unchanged.

  • statistics: one row per location with LOCATION, E_aug, V_tt, V_tc, V_cc, max_tt, max_tc, residual_df, authority and lambda_min_rel, from the final scoring of the returned placement.

  • diagnostics: per location, the location and its seed, the search status and phase statuses, objective and proxy calls, proposals, failed proposals, disconnected candidates and time_limit_hit.

  • contraction: per location, the k x s matrix whose entry (h, j) is the cross-line holding check h in field line j (field column j for "columns", field row j for "rows"), with rows in check-label order.

  • timing: per location, search, verification and total elapsed seconds, kept apart from the deterministic content.

  • metadata: the seed, RNG settings, package version and the complete effective parameters.

Details

Construction. The design is a complete nrows x ncols field. Every test entry occupies one plot and every check occupies s plots: exactly one in each of the s field lines along check_direction. Along the v cross-lines, no check is repeated and every cross-line holds between floor(k * s / v) and ceiling(k * s / v) check plots, at least one. This is the restricted contraction construction of Piepho and Williams (2026); square fields (v = s) include the square-array designs of Bailey and Haines (2025). Field coordinates and plot numbers are fixed at construction.

Model and objectives. Under the additive model with fixed row, column and entry effects and independent errors, the residual degrees of freedom are k * s - k - v - s + 2. Fields with fewer than 1 are rejected. Fields with fewer than 10 raise a warning: only adding a check or changing the number of rows or columns raises them. E_aug, V_tt and V_tc are reported for every location, whichever is optimized.

Search, budget and time limit. FielDHub searches the check positions with staged annealing; the search is FielDHub's own method, not part of the published construction. Each location runs one search with its own seed (the recorded seed plus the location index minus one) and at most budget objective calls. time_limit, when given, bounds each location's search phase only: final verification, randomization and field-book assembly always run to completion, and with l locations the call can take about l * time_limit seconds plus that work. A location stopped by the time limit records time_limit_hit = TRUE in its diagnostics. A cutoff reached before the search has produced any design raises a fieldhub_arc_search_error, as does a search that finds no connected start; there is no silent fallback to another method.

Randomization. After the search, the field lines and cross-lines are permuted at random, the check labels receive one random permutation, and the tests are assigned to the test plots at random. None of these steps changes an objective. The returned contraction and statistics describe this final, randomized placement.

Reproducibility

reproduce_design(x) and do.call(augmented_row_column, x$metadata$parameters) replay the design from its recorded parameters. Replay is exact (identical field book, contraction, statistics, diagnostics and parameters; only timing and the recorded package version are excluded) for evaluation-budget runs that did not hit time_limit, within the same software and numerical environment: the same FielDHub and R versions, BLAS/LAPACK library and thread count, and platform. A time_limit cutoff makes replay timing-dependent. In a different environment, replay gives a valid design with comparable statistics, which may be a different design.

Standalone reproduction code is available for the standard entry template at any size, and for any upload up to 200 rows. An upload whose ENTRY values are exactly 1, ..., k + n in row order is recorded as its check and test labels, with data = NULL; other uploads are recorded as uploaded, and above 200 rows the reproduction code falls back to the saved result (RDS).

References

Piepho, H.-P., and Williams, E. R. (2026). Rectangular augmented row-column designs generated from contractions. Biometrical Journal, 68(5), e70182. doi:10.1002/bimj.70182

Bailey, R. A., and Haines, L. M. (2025). Square array designs for unreplicated test treatments with replicated controls. Journal of Agricultural, Biological and Environmental Statistics. doi:10.1007/s13253-025-00699-1

See also

diagonal_arrangement, reproduce_design, design_arguments

Examples

# 4 checks and 48 tests in a 10 x 8 field; every check appears once in
# each field column. A small budget keeps the example fast.
x <- augmented_row_column(nrows = 10, ncols = 8, checks = 4,
                          check_direction = "columns", budget = 2000,
                          seed = 2026)
x$infoDesign$residual_df
#> [1] 12
x$statistics
#>   LOCATION     E_aug     V_tt     V_tc      V_cc   max_tt   max_tc residual_df
#> 1        1 0.5884851 3.502748 1.872188 0.2767563 4.120002 2.037172          12
#>     authority lambda_min_rel
#> 1 full_layout      0.1722068
head(x$fieldBook)
#>   ID  EXPT LOCATION YEAR PLOT ROW COLUMN CHECKS ENTRY TREATMENT CHECK_DIRECTION
#> 1  1 Expt1        1 2026  101   1      1      0     7        G7         columns
#> 2  2 Expt1        1 2026  102   1      2      3     3       CH3         columns
#> 3  3 Expt1        1 2026  103   1      3      1     1       CH1         columns
#> 4  4 Expt1        1 2026  104   1      4      4     4       CH4         columns
#> 5  5 Expt1        1 2026  105   1      5      0    30       G30         columns
#> 6  6 Expt1        1 2026  106   1      6      0     8        G8         columns
# Check plots per field column: each check once in every column
checks <- x$fieldBook[x$fieldBook$CHECKS > 0, ]
table(checks$TREATMENT, checks$COLUMN)
#>      
#>       1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
#>   CH1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1
#>   CH2 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1
#>   CH3 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1
#>   CH4 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1

# The same field turned through 90 degrees, with labelled checks
y <- augmented_row_column(nrows = 8, ncols = 10,
                          checks = c("Check A", "Check B", "Check C",
                                     "Check D"),
                          check_direction = "rows", objective = "E_aug",
                          budget = 2000, seed = 7)
y$contraction
#> $`1`
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] [,7] [,8]
#> [1,]   10    7    5    9    6    1    2    8
#> [2,]    8    3    9    6    4    2    5    7
#> [3,]    2   10    1    7    5    8    3    4
#> [4,]    9    1    4    3   10    6    8    2
#> 

# Replay from the recorded parameters
identical(reproduce_design(x)$fieldBook, x$fieldBook)
#> [1] TRUE
